name: outer town wall section, 3/4 top-down: wall-walk top with front parapet seen from above, ashlar front face pierced by a double round-arched canal water gate (voussoirs, keystones, a royal blue-and-gold shield on the middle pier), canal entering above and flowing out below
label: beodeul_city/capital/capital_watergate_s

surfaces.part: wall-walk top (pavers) with front parapet merlons
ashlar front face with double arched water gate, voussoirs and keystones
right tower top platform with crenellated parapet
right tower front face with arrow slits
flag on pole and hatch on tower floor

answer.evidence: The main wall section has a wall-walk top band of about 30 rows (49-78). It shows paver courses and a crenellated parapet, and ends in a dark front-edge line at row 79 followed by a light ledge and shadow. Below it is a tall ashlar front face of about 63 rows (80-143) pierced by two round arches over the canal. The right tower also has a visible floor and parapet top (rows 16-63) above its front face with a machicolation band. There is no isometric side face, so the view is a south-facing three-quarter view.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a stone wall with a canal gate, so the kind is close enough to the house references. Measured facts: 10 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10 for the references, so tile density is comparable. Near-flat coverage is 13% against 0% for both references, so there are some flat areas. Dark edge pixels are only 13% neutral, so the outlines are tinted rather than black. By eye, the ashlar blocks have per-stone variation, and the arches have voussoirs. However, the stone ramp is only about 4 steps of light grey, with a pale, uniform tone across the wall-walk and tower faces. The grass and water areas look like repeated patterned fills with little clump-level variation. The tower wall and the lower wall face have large regions of near-identical stone grey. The references use 5-6 steps with more grain on every surface. The candidate is clean and competent but visibly flatter and more uniform than the references, and the 13% flat coverage backs that up. Under the 'when in doubt, fail' rule, this fails.

surfaces.part: right tower roof platform with floor and crenellated parapet
flag on pole and hatch on tower platform
ashlar front face with double arched water gate and shield

answer.evidence: The wall has a wide wall-walk top (rows 49-65) in pink and cream paving. Below it is a crenellated parapet band (rows 66-79) that ends in a light front-edge line at about row 79-80 with dark shadow under it. Under that is a tall ashlar front face (rows ~81-142) with two round arches and the shield on the middle pier. The canal enters above and flows out below. The right tower also shows its top platform (rows 16-63) with floor and merlons, ending in an edge line and a dark machicolation band, then its front face below. The flag and hatch on the platform are decor.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate matches the references on the primary facts. It has 10 visible tones per tile against 12 and 10, and only 13% of its dark edge pixels are near-neutral, so the outlines lean tinted. Visually the ashlar blocks are shaded one by one in about 5 grey steps, with per-block highlights, joints and speckle. The grass has tufts, the water has rain streaks and foam, and the arches have voussoirs and a keystone. Near-flat coverage is 13% against 0% for the references, mainly on the tower top and parts of the parapet. The water gate and shield are also a little less detailed than the tile roofs, which have scallops and per-tile highlights. That puts it slightly below the references, but a careful artist would accept it next to them without it looking sticker-like.

surfaces.part: wall-walk top with paving and front parapet
right tower roof terrace with crenellations
canal water gate arches, voussoirs and shield in the ashlar face

answer.evidence: The main wall body has a wall-walk top over rows 49-78: pink and cream paving, then a crenellated parapet. A dark front-edge line at row 79 (L=90 at x=40, 80 and 119) closes it, and the ashlar front face with the double arched gate runs below it to about row 135 (roughly 56 rows). The right tower likewise has a terrace with merlons at the top (rows ~16-61) above its own front face. No isometric side face is drawn, since the tower and wall both show only their south faces. The canal reads as water above and below the wall.

styleAnswer.evidence: The measured facts put the candidate at 10 visible tones per tile, against 12 and 10 for the references, so it is at or near reference level. Only 13% of its pixels sit in flat 5x5 blocks, and only 13% of its dark edge pixels are neutral, so the outlines are tinted. By eye, the ashlar blocks are shaded one by one in several greys with mortar lines, and the voussoirs, keystones, crenellations and tower slits are separated by value rather than by a black line. The water carries ripple and foam texture, and the grass has tufts. The stone ramps run about 5 steps against 5-6 in the references. The wall-walk top and some grass patches are a little smoother and flatter than the references' per-tile grain, so density is a touch lower. Overall a careful artist would accept it next to the references.

surfaces.part: wall-walk top with paving and front parapet
flag and hatch on tower platform
ashlar front face with double arched water gate

answer.evidence: The wall-walk is a roughly 30-row paved band (rows 49-78) with a crenellated parapet. It ends in a dark front-edge line at row 79 (x=40, 80 and 119 all show L=90), and the ashlar face begins below it. The face runs about rows 80-143 and holds the two arches, the shield and the water. The right tower likewise has a platform (rows 16-62) with an edge line at row 63 and a machicolation band under it, then a long front face. The front face has well over 3 rows, so this is not a flat slab. No receding side face is drawn.

styleAnswer.evidence: The ashlar blocks are shaded one by one in about 5 grey steps (highlight, light, mid, shadow, deep joint), and the wall-walk top has per-block tone variation and speckle. Outlines and joints lean blue-grey or teal rather than black, which fits the measured 13% neutral share of dark edge pixels (references 7-9%). The arch voussoirs, the keystone and the shield on the pier carry readable detail. The canal has dark teal bands, rain streaks and foam at the gate, and the grass has tufts, so there are no large dead fills. Visible tones per tile are 10, against 12 and 10 for the references. Near-flat coverage is 13% against 0% for the references, which is a little flatter, mostly in the water bands and tower face. Overall it is comparable to the stone reference and would sit acceptably next to it, though slightly less textured than the richer timber house.
